label: J. Allen Hynek
narrative: J. Allen Hynek was the Air Force's scientific consultant on unidentified objects continuously from Project SIGN in 1948 through Blue Book's termination in 1969 — twenty-one years, longer than anyone else in the system. He was hired to explain sightings away as astronomical misidentifications and did so effectively for a decade. His conversion is the single best-documented insider defection of the legacy era. In March 1966, sent to Michigan after mass sightings near Dexter and Hillsdale, he offered swamp gas as a possible explanation for some cases; the press stripped the qualifiers, the explanation became a national joke, and Hynek concluded he had been used as the front for an institutional posture rather than an inquiry. He testified to the House Committee on Science and Astronautics on 29 July 1968 and by then was stating publicly that Blue Book was procedurally inadequate, under-resourced and 'totally inadequate' as a research effort — a public relations exercise with 'little or no research undertaken using the scientific method.' Hynek is the proof that the Air Force's own scientist concluded the Air Force was not investigating.
